name: Battle of the Hydaspes
note: The plan shows the fight after Alexander had crossed. The accounts do not say on which side of the river the armies stood or which way the field ran, so the river is drawn along the left edge and the Macedonians face right. Where Coenus's squadrons stood at the start, where the chariots stood along the front, and where the Macedonian phalanx stood while it held back are not stated and are placed by judgement. The accounts do not say where the Indian cavalry fled, so its flight is drawn a short way towards the elephants. Alexander's foot archers and light infantry are not drawn. Losses are not shown, since Arrian and Diodorus give different figures.

terrain.name: Hydaspes
terrain.quote: It took place on the banks of the Hydaspes River

units.name: Dahae horse archers
units.quote: Alexander commenced the battle by sending his Dahae horse archers to harass the Indian right-wing cavalry.

units.name: Companion cavalry
units.quote: His armoured Companion cavalry was sent to attack their outnumbered Indian counterparts on the left wing, with Alexander himself leading the charge as was his habit.

units.name: Coenus's cavalry squadrons
units.quote: but Coenus's squadrons promptly followed their movement and attacked them from the rear.

units.name: Macedonian phalanx
units.quote: having his phalanx hold back until the Indian cavalry had been neutralized.

units.name: Craterus's force
units.quote: Craterus and his force in the base camp had succeeded in crossing the river

units.name: Indian right-wing cavalry
units.quote: The Indians were poised with cavalry on both flanks, fronted by their chariots

units.name: Indian left-wing cavalry
units.quote: The Indians were poised with cavalry on both flanks, fronted by their chariots

units.name: Indian chariots
units.quote: The Indians were poised with cavalry on both flanks, fronted by their chariots

units.name: Indian war elephants
units.quote: war elephants stationed every fifty feet in front of them, to deter the Macedonian cavalry.

units.name: Indian infantry
units.quote: their center comprising infantry with war elephants stationed every fifty feet in front of them

phases.title: The armies draw up
phases.text: The Indians stood with cavalry on both flanks, chariots in front and infantry in the centre with elephants before it. Alexander judged the centre the strongest part and kept his phalanx back while his cavalry prepared to go for the flanks.
phases.quote: Alexander, noticing that Porus' disposition was strongest in the center, decided to attack with his cavalry first on the flanks

phases.title: The Macedonian cavalry strikes the Indian flanks
phases.text: The Dahae horse archers harassed the Indian right-wing cavalry, and the Companions, with Alexander leading, charged the Indian cavalry on the left wing, which was outnumbered.
phases.quote: Alexander commenced the battle by sending his Dahae horse archers to harass the Indian right-wing cavalry.

phases.title: The Indian right-wing cavalry is caught from behind
phases.text: The rest of the Indian cavalry rode over to help the hard-pressed left wing. Coenus's squadrons followed and struck them from the rear, so the Indian horsemen had to face two attacks at once.
phases.quote: The rest of the Indian cavalry galloped to the aid of their hard-pressed kinsmen from the right wing

phases.title: The Indian cavalry is routed
phases.text: The Indian horsemen tried to form a double phalanx, but the manoeuvre added to their confusion. They were routed and fled towards the safety of their elephants.
phases.quote: The Indian cavalry were thus routed, and fled to the safety of their elephants.

phases.title: The elephants advance and meet the phalanx
phases.text: The war elephants advanced and were met by the Macedonian phalanx. They caused heavy losses among the Macedonian foot, trampling and disorganising their dense lines, but the infantry kept up its resistance.
phases.quote: The war elephants now advanced against the Macedonian cavalry, only to be confronted by the Macedonian phalanx.

phases.title: The Indian cavalry sallies again and is repulsed
phases.text: While the elephants fought the phalanx, the Indian horsemen attempted another sally. Alexander's cavalry squadrons, which had all massed together, repulsed them once again.
phases.quote: Meanwhile, the Indian horsemen attempted another sally, only to be repulsed once again by Alexander's cavalry squadrons, who had all massed together.

phases.title: The elephants are driven back into their own lines
phases.text: The elephants were repulsed and fled back to their own lines. Many of their mahouts had been struck down, and the maddened animals trampled many of their own infantry and cavalry.
phases.quote: The elephants were eventually repulsed and fled back to their own lines.

phases.title: The phalanx advances and the cavalry charges from behind
phases.text: The Macedonian foot locked their shields and advanced on the confused enemy mass while the cavalry charged from the rear. The whole Indian army was put to rout.
phases.quote: Finally, the Macedonian pezhetairoi locked their shields and advanced upon the confused enemy mass

phases.title: Craterus crosses and pursues the fleeing Indians
phases.text: Meanwhile Craterus and his force in the base camp had succeeded in crossing the river. They arrived at the right moment and conducted a thorough pursuit of the fleeing Indians.
phases.quote: Meanwhile, Craterus and his force in the base camp had succeeded in crossing the river
